_comment_Logging: IO-07: EF Core logs every SQL command at Information, which on the club's Pi was ~35 KB a minute of container log with nobody using the stack (the workers poll). Warning here, so every environment but Development (which restates its own levels) is quiet; the host's json-file log is also capped per service in the compose files. Microsoft.AspNetCore.Hosting.Diagnostics at Warning keeps request lines - whose query strings can carry a stream ticket or a one-time link token - out of the log (BM-22, BP-18). Override per category with Logging__LogLevel__<category>.
_comment_ConnectionStrings: Development placeholder. Override via ConnectionStrings__DefaultConnection env var in all non-local environments.
_comment_Jwt: Secret is DELIBERATELY ABSENT here. It used to carry a committed placeholder, which meant the required-check in Program.cs never fired and a deployment that forgot Jwt__Secret signed every session token with a value published in this repository. The development value lives in appsettings.Development.json; every other environment sets Jwt__Secret. See Security/JwtSecretPolicy.cs.
_comment_Admins: Inherent administrators of this DEPLOYMENT. Whenever a user with one of these addresses exists in a club, that account holds club-admin rights in that club - applied at sign-in, so somebody who registers next month gets it too. It confers the admin flag and nothing else: never a password, never a verified address, never a club's approval, and never a user row in a club the person has not joined (a person with accounts at two clubs is an admin at both; a person with an account at neither is an admin at neither). DEPLOYMENT-OWNED, NOT CLUB-OWNED, which is why it is here and not in tenant_settings: a club editing the list of people who can administer every club on the deployment is the thing this list exists to be independent of. The club appoints its own admins from Admin -> Members, and those are untouched by this key. An empty array is a valid, ordinary configuration. Removing an address does NOT strip a live admin - that would turn a config edit into a lockout - it logs a warning instead; remove the rights in Admin -> Members. Not a secret, but security-relevant: editing it changes who administers the deployment. Entries are trimmed, lower-cased and de-duplicated; blanks and malformed addresses are ignored and named in a startup warning. Override with Admins__Emails__0, Admins__Emails__1, ... See Services/InherentAdmins.cs.
_comment_App: PublicBaseUrl is the DEPLOYMENT's address, which is the default club's (Tenancy:DefaultTenantSlug) when its host has no club label. Every other club's links (verify, reset, welcome, admin notices, PayFast return) use the same address with the club's slug as the first host label - https://crusaders.frostaura.net becomes https://kestrel.frostaura.net - unless the operator set tenants.PublicBaseUrl for it with `tenant set-url`. See Services/TenantLinks.cs.
_comment_Uploads: Bounds on the anonymous photo upload (BP-04), deployment-owned for the reason the rate limits are: they protect the disk every club shares. RecentBytesPerClub caps what one club's photo directory takes in over two hours (refused 503 uploads_paused past it); OrphanAfterMinutes is how old a photo no membership references must be before the sweep removes it (minimum 5).
_comment_Tenancy: A request's club is the one its token names, else the first label of its host, else - only on the anonymous auth, upload and invite routes - DefaultTenantSlug. The order is fixed in Multitenancy/TenantResolutionMiddleware.cs; there is no header-based resolution.
_comment_Biometric: Driver: 'Null' is the CI/development simulator, which matches the FIRST enrolled candidate - honoured only in Development and Testing. Anything else (and 'Null' anywhere else) is no reader at all: nothing enrols and nothing matches. No hardware driver exists yet. See Biometric/NoBiometricDevice.cs.
_comment_RateLimits: Per-minute ceilings. Deployment infrastructure rather than club policy, so these live here and not in tenant_settings: the limiter runs before tenant resolution and partitions by the client address the gateway forwarded, by the authenticated member for the auth policy, the writes policy (booking, players, play and desk writes: a token bucket of WritesBurst refilled at WritesPerMinute, never tighter than AuthPerMinute) and the global backstop (GlobalPerMinute per member; GlobalPerIpPerMinute per address for anonymous requests only), or by the club for the device policy - none of which is a tenant-scoped setting.
_comment_Gateway: Proxies whose X-Forwarded-For / -Proto / -Host headers the API believes. Addresses or CIDR networks. Default: loopback plus 172.29.83.0/24, the ipam subnet docker-compose.yml pins for the gateway container — change both together. It is a DELIMITED STRING, not an array, on purpose: .NET configuration merges arrays by index, so Gateway__TrustedProxies__0 over a three-entry array left the other two entries trusted and could not narrow the default. A scalar is replaced whole by Gateway__TrustedProxies=a,b, and the indexed form still works because there are no array children here to merge with. ForwardLimit is how many X-Forwarded-For hops may be walked back: 2 covers cloudflared in front of the gateway, and the middleware re-checks trust at each hop, so it cannot be abused by a client the API does not already trust.
_comment_Webhooks: SSRF guard. AllowPrivateNetworks disables it wholesale; false here for every environment, turned on in appsettings.Development.json only. PrivateNetworkAllowList is the carve-out CLAUDE.md requires for the lights controller: CIDRs, so a /32 admits one board rather than the whole private internet.
